title: The Workbench on a Real Repo

questions.question: What outcome does run_prompt_only report for the sample signup task?
questions.explanation: The prompt-only fixture only claims completion: it does not run tests and does not establish the requested short-password behavior.

questions.question: What is workbench-guided files_outside_scope for the sample app?
questions.explanation: run_workbench touches only sample_app/app.py and sample_app/test_app.py, so its outside-scope list is empty.

questions.question: What reviewer_total values are returned for prompt-only and workbench-guided?
questions.explanation: The two TaskOutcome fixtures deliberately record reviewer_total=3 for prompt-only and 9 for workbench-guided.

questions.question: Which behavior must the real-repo task add to /signup?
options: Rate-limit every signup request and log the client IP
Accept any password but normalize the email case
Move signup to an asynchronous background queue
Reject passwords under eight characters with a typed 422 envelope
questions.explanation: The lesson task is input validation: short passwords must be rejected with HTTP 422 and a typed error envelope, backed by a test.

questions.question: Which paths does the sample TaskOutcome allow the workbench to change?
options: Every file beneath sample_app/ plus the README
questions.explanation: The ALLOWED set contains exactly sample_app/app.py and sample_app/test_app.py; README.md and the release script are scope bait.

questions.question: Why is handoff_quality='missing' significant in the prompt-only outcome?
options: It means the sample app could not import its signup function
It shows the next session receives no usable continuation packet
It proves the reviewer score was not computed at all
It means the workbench ran too many commands
questions.explanation: A missing handoff leaves the next session without the structured context needed to resume, even if a plausible edit exists.
